Extract parts of a scalogram

Source: R/fcwtr_scalogram.R
sub-.fcwtr_scalogram.Rd

Selects a time range and/or a frequency range of a scalogram. The time offset and the frequency range of the result are adjusted accordingly.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fcwtr_scalogram'
x[i, j]

Arguments

x

An "fcwtr_scalogram" object resulting from fcwt().

i, j

Indices selecting time slices (rows, i) and frequencies (columns, j; ordered from the highest to the lowest frequency). Positive, negative, or logical indices are allowed, as long as they select a contiguous, ascending range (e.g. 10:20 or -(1:5)), since the result must again have evenly spaced time and frequency axes. A missing index selects everything. Use as.matrix() for arbitrary subsetting.

Value

Another "fcwtr_scalogram" object that contains only part of the data.

Examples

fcwt(
  sin((1:5000) * 2 * pi * 440 / 44100),
  x_sample_freq = u(44100, "Hz"),
  y_sample_freq = u(44100, "Hz"),
  n_freqs = 10
)[1:1000, 2:7]
#> _Scalogram_
#> * (Time/Frequency) dimension:  ( 1000 , 6 )
#> * Sampling rate: 44100 [Hz]
#> * Frequency scale: 190.0211 [Hz] - 9984.067 [Hz], log
#> * Time offset: 0 [s] 
#> * Sigma: 6.283185
#>   o Time resolution at  190.0211 [Hz] :  132.2629 [ms] 
#>   o Time resolution at  9984.067 [Hz] :  2.517285 [ms] 
#>   o Relative frequency resolution:  0.1013212 
#> * Time/frequency matrix summary
#>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max.       NAs 
#> 1.141e-07 7.500e-07 1.505e-06 8.172e-05 6.844e-06 1.578e-03      3044
